verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.75
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 5.75

verses.pali: 8. Yodhājīvavagga
verses.english: 8. Warriors

verses.pali: Paṭhamayodhājīvasutta
verses.english: Warriors (1st)

verses.pali: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, yodhājīvā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.

verses.pali: Katame pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati na santhambhati na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
verses.english: Firstly, one warrior falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

verses.pali: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo hoti.
verses.english: Some warriors are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is the first warrior found in the world.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust,

verses.pali: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
verses.english: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

verses.pali: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo hoti.
verses.english: Some warriors are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is the second warrior found in the world.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ sahati dhajaggaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

verses.pali: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
verses.english: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

verses.pali: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo hoti.
verses.english: Some warriors are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is the third warrior found in the world.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

verses.pali: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
verses.english: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

verses.pali: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo hoti.
verses.english: Some warriors are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck.

verses.pali: So taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
verses.english: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

verses.pali: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo hoti.
verses.english: Some warriors are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: These are the five warriors found in the world.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.

verses.pali: Katame pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: Firstly, one monk falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Kimassa rajaggasmiṁ?
verses.english: What is his ‘cloud of dust’?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suṇāti:
verses.english: It’s when a monk hears:

verses.pali: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti.
verses.english: ‘In such and such a village or town there’s a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

verses.pali: So taṁ sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: Hearing this, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Idamassa rajaggasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is his ‘cloud of dust’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
verses.english: I say that this individual is like the warrior who falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust.

verses.pali: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
verses.english: Some individuals are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust,

verses.pali: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: but at the mere sight of a banner’s crest he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Kimassa dhajaggasmiṁ?
verses.english: What is his ‘banner’s crest’?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva kho suṇāti:
verses.english: It’s when a monk doesn’t hear:

verses.pali: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti;
verses.english: ‘In such and such a village or town there’s a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

verses.pali: api ca kho sāmaṁ passati itthiṁ vā kumāriṁ vā abhirūpaṁ dassanīyaṁ pāsādikaṁ paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgataṁ.
verses.english: But he sees for himself a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

verses.pali: So taṁ disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: Seeing her, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Idamassa dhajaggasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is his ‘banner’s crest’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ;
verses.english: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust,

verses.pali: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
verses.english: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest.

verses.pali: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
verses.english: Some individuals are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

verses.pali: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Kimassa ussāraṇāya?
verses.english: What is his ‘turmoil’?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā ūhasati ullapati ujjagghati uppaṇḍeti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She smiles, chats, laughs, and teases him.

verses.pali: So mātugāmena ūhasiyamāno ullapiyamāno ujjagghiyamāno uppaṇḍiyamāno saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
verses.english: He falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

verses.pali: Sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
verses.english: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Idamassa ussāraṇāya.
verses.english: This is his ‘turmoil’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ;
verses.english: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

verses.pali: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
verses.english: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil.

verses.pali: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
verses.english: Some individuals are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ;
verses.english: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

verses.pali: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
verses.english: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

verses.pali: Kimassa sampahārasmiṁ?
verses.english: What is his ‘blows are struck’?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

verses.pali: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno sikkhaṁ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṁ anāvikatvā methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevati.
verses.english: Without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.

verses.pali: Idamassa sampahārasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is his ‘blows are struck’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati;
verses.english: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, but is killed or injured when blows are struck.

verses.pali: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
verses.english: Some individuals are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ, so taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
verses.english: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

verses.pali: Kimassa saṅgāmavijayasmiṁ?
verses.english: What is his ‘victory in battle’?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

verses.pali: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno viniveṭhetvā vinimocetvā yena kāmaṁ pakkamati.
verses.english: But he disentangles and frees himself, and goes wherever he wants.

verses.pali: So vivittaṁ senāsanaṁ bhajati araññaṁ rukkhamūlaṁ pabbataṁ kandaraṁ giriguhaṁ susānaṁ vanapatthaṁ abbhokāsaṁ palālapuñjaṁ.
verses.english: He frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

verses.pali: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
verses.english: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

verses.pali: So abhijjhaṁ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṁ parisodheti;
verses.english: Giving up covetousness for the world, he meditates with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

verses.pali: byāpādapadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī byāpādapadosā cittaṁ parisodheti;
verses.english: Giving up ill will and malevolence, he meditates with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

verses.pali: thinamiddhaṁ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṁ parisodheti;
verses.english: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, he meditates with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

verses.pali: uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṁ parisodheti;
verses.english: Giving up restlessness and remorse, he meditates without restlessness, his mind peaceful inside, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

verses.pali: vicikicchaṁ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṅkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṁ parisodheti.
verses.english: Giving up doubt, he meditates having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

verses.pali: So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe
verses.english: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

verses.pali: vivicceva kāmehi …pe…
verses.english: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption …

verses.pali: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

verses.pali: So evaṁ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṁ khayañāṇāya cittaṁ abhininnāmeti.
verses.english: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti,
verses.english: He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

verses.pali: ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ jānato evaṁ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati,
verses.english: Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

verses.pali: vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
verses.english: When it is freed, he knows it is freed.

verses.pali: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

verses.pali: Idamassa saṅgāmavijayasmiṁ.
verses.english: This is his ‘victory in battle’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ, so taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati;
verses.english: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

verses.pali: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
verses.english: Some individuals are like that.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
verses.english: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsū”ti.
verses.english: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”

verses.pali: Pañcamaṁ.
